cells.location: Cheruvu Madhavaram.
cells.place: Collector of Krishna District.
cells.remarks: Records that king Kali-Vittara alias Kali-Vishnuvardhana, having installed god Nagateśvara-bhaṭṭāraka, together with a nagara, granted to the god some land probably purchased from Droṇakurru-bhaṭṭa of Kāśyapa-gotra, and emanated the copper-plate to the village of Pāganūru, situated in the Guddavādi-vishaya and a disciple of Amṛtaśōmā-āchārya who was a disciple of Balaśōma-bhagavanta. The grant is stated to have been made on the occasion of Uttarāyaṇa-saṅkramaṇa.

cells.date: Śaka 1105, Sōbhakṛit, Āśvayuja, Amāvāsyā, Monday, Vyatīpāta = 1183 A.D., October 17, f.d.t. 41.
cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Kukkauṇru, the abode of the goddess Jyeṣṭhadēvī situated in Beluvala-300 by the king, as sarvamānya to 1,000 Mahā-Brāhmaṇas belonging to various gōtras. The document was composed by the poet-laureate (kavi-cakravartin) Sōmanātha, son of Lakṣmīdhara and engraved by Rāja-vijñānin Paṇḍayya. There is a Kannada endorsement recording a minor gift of land and a house by Divākara-daṇḍanāyaka of Kōṭhāra. Published in Ind. Ant., Vol. IV, pp. 274 ff.

cells.location: Shri Rama Bhat, Ikkēri, Sagara Taluk, Shimoga District, Mysore — Karnataka
cells.place: Paper manuscript of a Sāndi.
cells.remarks: Records an order of Veṅkaṭappa-nāyaka pertaining to the privileges of rights, as being a right, such as dēvadāna, samprōkshana, bhōkshana and adhishṭhāna in the temples of Ikkeri, Sāgara, Keladi, Banavāsi, Gutti, Anantapura and Bidarūru, of Liṅga-bhaṭṭa of Ikkēri. The rights of this Sāndi are further held by Channavīra-bhaṭṭa and others of Anantapura. The order states that the Pārupattēgāra and Sēnābōvas of the respective areas should put down the mischievous elements and set things right. In characters of about the 17th century.

cells.location: Elanūru

See Nos. 18-19 below.

cells.location: Nittūru †
cells.place: Slab set up in front of the Chennakēśava temple in the same village (as Nīlakaṇṭhēśvara temple) (as Nīlakaṇṭhēśvara temple). †
cells.remarks: Registers gift of lands to god Chennakēśava of Nittūru by Rāmaḷinga-nāyṇingāru, son of Pennasani-Tin.mā-nay-iningāru, at Nittūru, a village in Chinabadi-śīma, granted to him as umbali by Tiru-malai-nāyningāru, son of Jakampūṇḍi Pedi-nāyningāru. Most of the lands were, as the record says, ref obtained by the latter from Rāmarāja-Tirumalarājaya-dēva-mahārāja. The gift was made on the occasion of Kṛishṇa-jayanti. The record contains two more grants made on the same day, one of them being that of the latter in the year Rākshasa (Śaka 1477) by the kāpus (farmers) and the karaṇas (accountants) of Nittūru, Gollapalle and Vēmulapalle, the former granting some lands of the latter grant to the rāyavēkāra officer for the worship of the deities in the village. The reverse of the slab gives an elaborate schedule of assignments of the gift land for the various items of offerings, of which one was Bhāgavata-śēva and another the chanting of the mantra-pushpam.

cells.remarks: Damaged. cells.location: Mūdinūr †
cells.place: Virabhadra temple. Slab kept in the temple.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. States that Rēvaya Dvēdi Chaṭṭōpādhyāya Sōmayāji who received the gift of the village Mūdeyanūr on the occasion of the performance of Brahmāṇḍa-kratu by the king, bestowed it on twenty learned Brāhmaṇas, constituting it into an agrahāra, and provided for the worship, etc., of the deity Kēśavadēva, and of the temple built in the village. cells.location: YALBARGI TALUK Kuknūr
cells.place: Mahāmāya temple. Slab set up in the mukhamanḍapa of the temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1100, Vilāmbi, Bhādrapada amāvāsyā, Monday, solar eclipse=1178 A.D., September 13, Wednesday (not Monday), Solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers an endowment of the village Saḷagara situated in Kukkanūr to the goddess Mahāmāya, the god Amṛita of Jyēshṭhā and Sōmēśvara by Dhaṁmagi-daṇḍanāyaka the governor of Belvaḷa, with the king's approval. The gift was entrusted into the hands of Siddhānti Kāḷēśvara who was the priest of the Sindas of Yalbargi and the superintendent of the temples. The record contains a lengthy poetic description of the goddess Jyēshṭhā and the eminence of Kāḷēśvara who belonged to the Kāḷāmukha line of teachers from Sūṇḍi.

cells.location: Śrīraṅgam
cells.place: Raṅganāthasvāmin temple, Kaśalyāmbi shrine, south wall.
cells.date: Śaka 1490, Vibhava, 15, Saturday, Śravishṭha=1508 A.D., August 7, Saturday, 75, '69.
cells.remarks: Records a grant of a number of villages as tiruviḍaiyāṭṭam yielding a total amount of 3500 pon by Tirumalaidēva-mahārāja of the Ātrēya gōtra, Āpastamba sūtra and Yajuh śākha for expenses towards various services specified. Among the villages are the ones at Kōṭṭai, Sōmanāthapuram, etc., and among kkuḍi, Veḷvattikkuḍi, Nattamangalam, etc., and among the services enumerated are the car festival on the day of Viśākha, the natal star of the donor, the Mahānavami festival in the goddess, and the daily food offerings in the temple, which is stated to be received in the Śrīraṅganārāyaṇan-tirumaṇḍapam. Also records additional grants for services in the names of Krishṇappa-nāyakkar, Achyutappa-nāyakkar and Guṇḍin-cheṭṭiyār. Mentions Eṭṭūr Tiru-malaikolundu-tātāchcharyār and specifies his share in the daily offerings.

cells.location: MADRAS †
cells.place: Koṭṭāram, same wall, below No. 365 above. wall of the paddy storage room †
cells.date: Śaka 1411, Saumya, Śrāvaṇa śu. 11, Friday=1489 A.D., August 7, Friday, 22.
cells.language: Sanskrit verse in Grantha and Tamil.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of the village Muṇḍambāṭi alias Śrīraṅganallūr in Paṭṭaiya-nāḍu as tiruviḍaiyāṭṭam to the god. The Sanskrit verse delineates the chief's genealogy as: Kulikāla of the solar race, in his family there was one Tikkana, his son Manmasiddha, his son (from Śrīdēvī) Tammuasiddhī who was the younger brother (anujanmā) of Manmasiddha. The gift village and the district in which it lay are mentioned respectively as Mōḍamā and Paṇṭa-rāṣṭra-viṣaya. It is stated that the record was engraved in the temple at Tiruppākkadal in a similar record may be engraved in the temple at Tiruppākkadal in Nollūr (See In. N.D., Nellore No. 75; S.I.I., Vol. V, No. 500).

cells.location: MADRAS †
cells.place: Fifth prākāra, east wall, north end, opposite the 1000-pillared maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Purports to be an order of the deity ratifying the proposals made in the 9th year of the reign of Vīra-Rāmanāthadēva by Echi-bhaṭṭan of Kausika-gōtra, the Kuḍinār-śāstai of the temple, that since all the temple lands are being neglected, servants made a representation to the god in respect of the Lakshmīnārāyaṇap-Perumāḷ temple (1) as a protective measure, a row of house-sites be given to deserving brāhmaṇas, the deity having shown all these, (?) the temple (?) as the income from the existing endowments to the temple was found inadequate for maintaining worship and offerings in it, some more lands from Guṇaśīla-chaturvēdimangalam be endowed for the purpose in the temple treasury. Echi-bhaṭṭan deposited 7500 kāśu in the temple treasury, and one of the signatories of the document figures Pallavan Vilupparaiyan.
